subject: HIN
label: Grade 01
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 01 Hindi, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Letters and sounds
modules.outcome: say and write Hindi vowels and consonants
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Letters and sounds', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: say and write Hindi vowels and consonants. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Letters and sounds' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: say and write Hindi vowels and consonants, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Echo: sound at 340 m/s returns after 2 s, so it travelled 680 m there and back, and the wall is 340 m away. Method: Model run for 'Letters and sounds'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Say and write Hindi vowels and consonants: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Say the first vowels: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ए ऐ ओ औ. Say each sound slowly: a, aa, i, ee, u, oo, e, ai, o, au. Trace each letter in the air with your finger, and write the top line (shirorekha) first.
Step 2, Link vowels to words. अ से अनार [A for pomegranate], आ से आम [Aa for mango], इ से इमली [I for tamarind], उ से उल्लू [U for owl]. Say the full line each time, like a chant: अ से अनार।

Step 3, Say the first consonants: क ख ग घ. क से कमल [K for lotus], ख से खरगोश [Kh for rabbit], ग से गमला [G for flower pot], घ से घर [Gh for house]. Notice that each consonant carries a short a sound.

Step 4, Write with a headline. Every letter in क, ख, ग, घ hangs from a line drawn on top, called शिरोरेखा [the headline]. Write each letter three times: क क क, ख ख ख. Then read your line aloud: कमल, खरगोश, घर.

Step 5, Fix an error. A learner writes the letters of कमल without the top line and reads क as k with no vowel. Correction: draw the line on top of every letter, and say each consonant with its short a: ka-ma-la, then read the whole word as कमल [lotus].
Step 6, Your turn: say and write च छ ज with one word each. Model answer: च से चम्मच [spoon], छ से छाता [umbrella], ज से जहाज़ [ship]. Write each letter three times with its headline.

modules.title: Matras: short and long vowel signs
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Matras: short and long vowel signs', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read words with matras. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Matras: short and long vowel signs' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read words with matras, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Short and long vowel signs change the sound: ka, kaa, ki, kee. Read: kamal, kaam, kitaab. Method: Model run for 'Matras: short and long vowel signs'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read words with matras: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Meet the vowel signs on क. क (ka), का (kaa), कि (ki), की (kee), कु (ku), कू (koo), के (ke), कै (kai), को (ko), कौ (kau). The signs are matras: ा ि ी ु ू े ै ो ौ. Say each syllable aloud.

Step 2, Read words with long aa. काम [work], नाम [name], आम [mango], घास [grass]. The sign ा is a straight line after the letter. Compare कल [tomorrow] with काल [time]; the matra makes the sound longer.
Step 3, Short and long i, u. किताब [book] has the short ि, दीदी [elder sister] has the long ी, पुल [bridge] has the short ु, फूल [flower] has the long ू. The long sounds are held a little longer.
Step 4, Read words with e, ai, o, au. मेला [fair], तैरना [to swim], मोर [peacock], चौका [kitchen platform]. Sentence: मोर नाचता है। [The peacock dances.] Point at each matra as you read.

Step 5, Fix an error. A learner reads कि as ik, because the short i sign is written before the letter. Correction: ि is written before but read after the consonant, so कि is ki. Write किताब and read ki-taab.

Step 6, Your turn: read and write the words for mango, flower and book with their matras. Model answer: आम, फूल, किताब. Then add the correct matra: प_नी (water) should be पानी, using the long aa sign.

modules.title: Simple words and objects
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Simple words and objects', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: read and write simple words. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.

Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: read and write simple words, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: मेरा नाम अमन है। मैं स्कूल जाता हूँ। यह मेरी किताब है। शब्द: कलम, किताब, गेंद। Method: Model run for 'Simple words and objects'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Read and write simple words: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Read two-letter words with no matras: जल [water], कल [tomorrow or yesterday], नल [tap], फल [fruit], घर [house], पल [a moment]. Sound out each consonant with its short a, then say the whole word smoothly.
Step 2, Add objects found in the classroom: कलम [pen], मेज़ [table], कुर्सी [chair], किताब [book], बस्ता [school bag]. Touch each object as you say its name, and read the label card aloud.
Step 3, Make sentences with है [is]. यह कलम है। [This is a pen.] वह घर है। [That is a house.] यह मेज़ है। [This is a table.] Replace the object with other words from your list.
Step 4, Short question and answer. यह क्या है? [What is this?] यह फल है। [This is a fruit.] वह क्या है? [What is that?] वह नल है। [That is a tap.] Ask your partner five times.
Step 5, Fix an error. A learner writes कमल when they mean pen. Correction: कलम is pen and कमल is lotus; the letters म and ल have swapped places. Read the word aloud to check meaning: क-ल-म is pen.
Step 6, Your turn: write one sentence about a chair and one about a school bag. Model answer: यह कुर्सी है। यह बस्ता है। [This is a chair. This is a school bag.] Check the headline over every letter.

modules.title: Rhymes
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Rhymes', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: recite short rhymes. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Rhymes' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: recite short rhymes, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: कविता की पंक्तियों में तुक खोजें (जैसे आम और शाम), कवि का भाव बताएँ और भावार्थ अपने शब्दों में लिखें। Method: Model run for 'Rhymes'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Recite short rhymes: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Listen to a short rhyme I made: नन्ही चींटी, चली कतार, दाना लेकर, घर के द्वार। [The little ant walked in a line, carrying a grain to the door of home.] Clap once on each stressed word.
Step 2, Find the rhyming words. कतार and द्वार end with the same sound आर. Other rhyming pairs: आम and शाम, बाग and आग, पल and जल. Say each pair twice and clap the rhythm.
Step 3, Learn the rhyme line by line. First say नन्ही चींटी, then चली कतार. Next say दाना लेकर, then घर के द्वार। Repeat the lines slowly, then at a steady walking speed, with hands marking the beat.
Step 4, Add actions. For नन्ही चींटी hold up a tiny finger. For चली कतार march on the spot. For दाना लेकर pretend to lift a grain. For घर के द्वार point to a door. Recite together as a group.
Step 5, Fix an error. A child says दाना लेकर, कतार चली, changing the line order and losing the rhyme. Correction: keep the order नन्ही चींटी, चली कतार so that कतार and द्वार end the pair of lines.
Step 6, Your turn: make a two-line rhyme using आम and शाम. Model answer: मीठा आम, खाऊँ सुबह-शाम। [Sweet mango, I eat it morning and evening.] Recite it three times with a clap.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Letters and sounds), and at which Bloom level is it?
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Rhymes) run?
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
One page in your learning book. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
